newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metsa-Serla down on pulp price gloom.
newsitem.headline: Metsa-Serla down on pulp price gloom.

text.p: Shares in Finnish forestry group Metsa-Serla fell sharply on a broadly weak market on Friday amid heightened uncertainties over prospects for pulp price hikes, brokers said.
At 1300/1100 GMT, Metsa-Serla B was down 1.30 markka, or almost four percent. Volume was a fair 2.6 million markka, or three percent of bourse turnover in a thinly traded session.
"This is due to the uncertainty over whether planned price rises will go through after the pulp inventories figures came in somewhat higher than expected," one broker said.
Those figures showed Norscan (North American and Scandinavian) pulp inventories up by 185,000 tonnes in November.

Earlier in the day, pulp-maker Metsa-Botnia -- which Metsa-Serla and its parent owns (53 percent) together with UPM-Kymmmene (47 percent) -- said it would refrain from a planned pulp price hike "for the time being."

Other forestries also slid, though by less than Metsa-Serla. UPM-Kymmene traded down 1.40 markka, or about 1.5 percent at 92.80 markka and Enso R was off 0.60 markka, or about 1.6 percent, at 35.90 markka.
